name: National University of Singapore
description: The National University of Singapore is a public research university founded in 1905 as the Straits Settlements and Federated Malay States Government Medical School, making it Singapore's oldest university. It is a comprehensive university with faculties spanning medicine, law, engineering, computing, business, science and the arts.
whyIncluded: One of Singapore's Ministry of Education (MOE)-funded Autonomous Universities and the country's largest, so it is the primary local benchmark against which overseas fees are compared.

programmes.name: Master of Computing (Computer Science Specialisation)
programmes.summary: Programme total spread over 1.5 years, including 9% GST. Not government-subsidised; Citizens and PRs get a 40% NUS rebate. Miscellaneous fees are extra.
programmes.notes: Self-funded (not MOE Tuition Grant) programme. Total tuition of S$69,215 incl. 9% GST for the Aug 2027 intake (up to 40 Units), divided by the 1.5-year full-time candidature; the same fee applies to all nationalities. Citizen/PR: the programme page does not print a figure, but it is on NUS's list for the Master's by Coursework Enhanced Tuition Fee Rebate (masters.nus.edu.sg; FAQ dated 3 Sep 2026), a 40% rebate for Singapore Citizens/PRs admitted in AY2024-AY2028, so the SC/PR figure is 60% of the published fee (S$41,529 incl. GST, /1.5). History (added/confirmed 2026-10-04 from Wayback Machine captures of this official fee page, read through the translate.goog mirror of web.archive.org): Aug 2026 intake: capture 20250910012110, 'Semester 1, AY2026/2027 (August 2026 Intake) onwards ... Tuition Fees (including prevailing GST 9%) S$67,144' (up to 40 Units), replacing the earlier aggregator-only figure (same amount); international row S$67,144 / 1.5 = S$44,762.67. Aug 2025 intake: capture 20250219210600, 'Semester 1, AY2025/2026 (August 2025 Intake) onwards ... Tuition Fees (including prevailing GST 9%) S$61,040.00' (up to 40 Units); international row S$61,040 / 1.5 = S$40,693.33. Aug 2024 intake: capture 20240722195138, 'Semester 1, AY2024/2025 (August 2024 Intake) onwards – MComp Programme (with Specialisations) ... Tuition Fees (including prevailing GST 9%): $57,279.50' (up to 40 Units); international row S$57,279.50 / 1.5 = S$38,186.33. The citizen and pr history rows are DERIVED as 60% of those totals (2026: S$40,286.40, 2025: S$36,624, 2024: S$34,367.70, each / 1.5), applying the NUS Master's by Coursework Enhanced Tuition Fee Rebate of 40% for Singapore Citizens/PRs admitted in AY2024-AY2028 (masters.nus.edu.sg FAQ), the same derivation as the current tiers; the 2025 and 2026 captures name the 'Enhanced Tuition Fee Rebate' on the page, while the 2024 capture refers to the 'SoC Tuition Fee Subsidy' for Singapore Citizens/PRs without stating its amount, so the 2024 SC/PR rows rest on the NUS-wide rebate statement rather than on a figure printed on the 2024 page. The retired MComp (AI) page shows the same S$57,279.50 for its last intake, AY2024/25. Excludes Miscellaneous Student Fees.

programmes.name: MSc in Finance
programmes.summary: Total fee for the programme (about 12 to 16 months), including 9% GST. Citizens and PRs get a 40% NUS rebate. Figure read from a third-party copy of the university's page. Miscellaneous fees extra.
programmes.notes: Self-funded (not MOE Tuition Grant) programme. Whole-programme fee for the Aug 2027 intake (AY2027/28) on the official page: S$71,000 before GST = S$77,390 incl. 9% GST, same for all nationalities (NUS alumni get a 20% rebate). Citizen/PR: the page prints no SC/PR figure, but MSc (Finance) is on NUS's list for the Master's by Coursework Enhanced Tuition Fee Rebate (40% for SC/PR admitted in AY2024-AY2028; masters.nus.edu.sg, FAQ dated 3 Sep 2026), so the SC/PR figure is 60% of the published fee. Full-time takes about 12-16 months. The official page (mscfin.nus.edu.sg) still blocks bots (Incapsula challenge page to direct requests on 2026-10-01), so it was read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-10-01, hence sourceType secondary. The 2026 history (S$75,210 incl. 9% GST = S$69,000 before GST, Aug 2026 intake) is a secondary figure first taken from educatly and the SC/PR entries apply the same 40% rebate; re-checked on 2026-10-02: educatly.com and mim-essay.com both reproduce the official page's 'August 2026 Intake' block verbatim (acceptance fee S$10,900 + two instalments of S$32,155 = S$75,210) and search-engine snippets of the official page show the same text, so the row is kept. The official page now shows only the 2027 intake. Aug 2024 / Aug 2025 intake fees could not be found on 2026-10-02: the Wayback Machine's captures of the official fee page (2024-07-23, 2024-09-16, 2025-01-24, 2025-04-20) are Incapsula bot-challenge pages rather than the page itself (the 2025-04-20 capture was retrieved and checked; the others are the same ~5 KB size), Common Crawl holds the same block pages, the official 'NUS MSc in Finance' 2025 brochure PDF (mscfin.nus.edu.sg/wp-content/uploads/sites/118/2026/01/MFIN-Brochure-2025-WEBRES-Edited-V2-1.pdf, retrieved directly) prints only the S$100 application fee and refers readers to the website, and mastersportal.com shows an older official fee text ('Before GST S$66,000.00; inclusive of 9% GST, with effect from 1 Jan 2024, S$71,940.00') with no intake label, so it cannot be assigned to a specific intake and is not recorded; no 2024/2025 rows are recorded. Excludes Miscellaneous Student Fees. Second pass, 2026-10-05: still no source ties a fee to the Aug 2024 or Aug 2025 intake, so no rows. Checked: (1) Common Crawl CC-MAIN-2023-50 to CC-MAIN-2025-30 for mscfin.nus.edu.sg/ (256 captures, including /faq/what-are-the-tuition-fees/ and /fees-finances/*), bschool.nus.edu.sg/msc-finance-old/ (Apr 2024 captures, including /fees-finances/), and nus.edu.sg/registrar/administrative-policies-procedures/graduate/graduate-fees (Mar, Jun, Aug, Dec 2024 and Apr 2025): every record is a ~1 KB Incapsula block page. (2) NUS Registrar 'gdtuitioncurrent.pdf' (Common Crawl 2025-07-10, AY2025/26, updated May 2025) covers government-subsidised graduate programmes only; MSc (Finance) is self-funded and not listed. (3) nusgs.nus.edu.sg/programmes/m-sc-in-finance-coursework is bot-blocked, and r.jina.ai gets a CAPTCHA. (4) Official brochures reachable directly from wp-content: 'FIN_WebBrochure2023_compressed.pdf' (uploaded 2024/04) and 'FINANCE-Webres_June2024_compressed.pdf' (created 13 Jun 2024) both say 'Please refer to our website for details on fees' and print only the S$100 application fee. (5) The mastersportal lead (mastersportal.com/studies/300687/finance.html): the Common Crawl/Wayback capture of 2024-05-30 shows 'Before GST S$66,000.00; Inclusive of 9% GST, with effect from 1 Jan 2024 S$71,940.00' next to 'Starting 2025-08-12', but the 2025-04-24 capture shows the same text next to 'Starting 2026-08-12', a stale figure since the official Aug 2026 fee is S$69,000 before GST. The Dec 2022 capture shows S$60,000 with 'Starting 2023-08-01'. So S$66,000 was published some time between Dec 2022 and May 2024 and was never refreshed. 'With effect from 1 Jan 2024' describes the GST rate change (66,000 x 1.09 = 71,940), not a fee start date, and the text could cover the Aug 2023 or the Aug 2024 intake. The page did not change when the fee did, so it cannot fix the Aug 2025 fee either, and the with-effect-from rule does not give an intake. (6) topuniversities.com captures (2022-07: 'Fees 60000-'; 2024-06, 2025-03, 2025-09: '66,000 SGD') carry no intake label and show the same staleness. Not estimated. Final sweep 2026-10-06: still no 2024/2025 rows. New sources tried: Wayback CDX for mscfin.nus.edu.sg/fees-finances/* (2023-2025) lists only 587-1,310-byte captures (Incapsula block pages); NUS Business School staging copies under bschool.nus.edu.sg (mscfin-qat, mfin-qat, msc-fin-qat, msc-finance-old, mscfin-old) return 404; the live staging page bschool.nus.edu.sg/msgfin-qat/fees-finances/programme-fees shows 'Academic Year 2024/2025' S$60,000 / S$65,400 but belongs to the MSc in Sustainable and Green Finance, not this programme; admitscholar.com (published 20 Oct 2025) quotes S$71,000 / S$77,390 with no intake label (it equals the current Aug 2027 figure), and search-engine summaries that attach S$69,000 to an 'August 2025 intake' are paraphrases of the official Aug 2026 block. Not estimated.

programmes.name: Master of Laws (LLM, General)
programmes.summary: Tuition for the one-year programme. Citizens and PRs pay the Ministry of Education (MOE) subsidised rate; international students pay the full fee including 9% GST. Fees may change each year. Miscellaneous fees extra.
programmes.notes: Tuition fees per annum for students matriculating in AY2026/27 from NUS Law's fee page ('LLM (General) / Corporate & Financial Services Law / International & Comparative Law / Intellectual Property & Technology Law' row). Citizen S$9,600 and PR S$17,050 are the MOE-subsidised rates, excl. GST (GST subsidised by MOE). International students are not MOE-subsidised: S$40,250 incl. 9% GST (a Singapore Citizen not taking the subsidy pays S$38,350). The specialist LLMs (Maritime Law, Asian Legal Studies, International Arbitration & Dispute Resolution, International Business Law) are self-funded at S$42,550 / S$38,940 incl. GST for all nationalities. A non-refundable acceptance fee of S$3,270 (incl. GST) is offset against tuition, so it is not a one-off fee. The page says fees are subject to change each AY; one-year programme. History (students admitted in August 2025) from the NUS Law 'Masters Programmes 2026' brochure PDF: S$9,600 / S$16,400 / S$37,100, confirmed by the Registrar's graduate fee PDF (gdtuitioncurrent.pdf, 'Updated as of June 2026'), whose cohort table 'Law' coursework row for students admitted in AY2025/2026 gives the same figures. 2024 history from the same Registrar PDF's cohort table for students admitted in AY2024/2025 ('Law' coursework row): SC S$9,600, PR S$15,750 (MOE-subsidised, excl. GST), international S$37,100 (incl. GST). Current figures also match the Registrar PDF's AY2026/2027 'Law' coursework row (9,600 / 17,050 / 38,350 / 40,250). Excludes Miscellaneous Student Fees.

programmes.name: Doctor of Medicine (MD, Duke-NUS Medical School)
programmes.summary: Yearly tuition, fixed for the four-year degree. Government-subsidised; international rate includes 9% GST. Graduates must work 4 to 5 years in Singapore public healthcare. Read from a third-party copy of the page.
programmes.notes: Graduate-entry, four-year MD at Duke-NUS Medical School (a school of NUS). Annual tuition for students admitted in Academic Year 2026-2027, from Duke-NUS's 'Tuition Fees for Doctor of Medicine (MD)' section; the fees are MOE-approved and government-subsidised and are fixed for the four-year duration of study. Citizen S$50,050 and PR S$68,150: 'GST subsidy provided' (i.e. excl. GST, GST subsidised by MOE). International S$99,900: inclusive of 9% GST. All MD graduates serve a service commitment (bond) in the public healthcare sector: 4 years for Singapore Citizens, 5 years for PRs and international graduates. The NUS Registrar's graduate fee PDF refers readers to Duke-NUS's own site for these fees. duke-nus.edu.sg blocks bots (Incapsula), so the page was read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-10-01, hence sourceType secondary. Duke-NUS publishes only the current intake's fees live, so the history comes from Wayback Machine captures of this same official page (read 2026-10-04 through the translate.goog mirror of web.archive.org; the Wayback CDX index shows that captures of about 19-22 KB are the real page while the ~1 KB ones are Incapsula bot-challenge pages). AY2025-2026 intake: capture 20250617210553, 'Tuition Fees for Doctor of Medicine (MD)', 'Academic Year 2025-2026': Singapore Citizens SGD 50,050 (GST subsidy provided), Singapore Permanent Residents SGD 66,150 (GST subsidy provided), International Students SGD 93,400 (inclusive of GST). AY2024-2025 intake: captures 20240919042818 and 20250430022711, 'Academic Year 2024-2025': Singapore Citizens SGD 49,050 (GST subsidy provided), Singapore Permanent Residents SGD 63,600 (GST subsidy provided), International Students SGD 85,700 (inclusive of GST). Both captures also state 'For the MD programme, tuition fees are fixed for the four-year duration of study'. These match the unlabelled S$50,050 / S$66,150 / S$93,400 figures in a November 2024 press article. Excludes Miscellaneous Student Fees, which Duke-NUS bills at the NUS graduate rates.

programmes.name: Master of Psychology (Clinical)
programmes.summary: Total fee for the 2-year programme, split per year, including GST. Citizens and PRs get a 10% NUS rebate. Figure read from a third-party copy of the university's page. Miscellaneous fees are extra.
programmes.notes: Self-funded (not MOE-subsidised) 2-year (24-month) full-time coursework programme, annual August intake (NUS Graduate School programme page). FASS 'Fees' page for graduate coursework programmes, 'Self-funded Programmes' table: tuition for students 'regardless of nationality, admitted in AY2026-2027', Master of Psychology (Clinical) S$83,850 per programme, incl. 9% GST. Annual figure = S$83,850 / 2 = S$41,925 (international tier). Citizen/PR: note 5 on the same page says this programme is excluded from the 40% Enhanced Tuition Fee Rebate but gets the NUS Master's Degree by Coursework Tuition Fee Rebate of 10% for Singaporeans and PRs (20% for NUS alumni of any nationality, not applied), so SC/PR = S$83,850 x 0.9 / 2 = S$37,732.50; the programme FAQ also says the 40% rebate does not apply and the 10% one does. Cohort-based fee system (fees fixed for the intake cohort). fass.nus.edu.sg blocks bots, so the current page was read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-10-05, hence sourceType secondary; the Wayback Machine capture of the programme page dated 1 Nov 2025 (20251101230951) also states 'AY2026/27 SGD 83,850' for the 2-year programme. History from Wayback Machine captures of the department's programme page (fass.nus.edu.sg/psy/master-of-psychology-clinical/), read 2026-10-05: capture 20250220105417 'Tuition Fees (inclusive of prevailing GST): AY2025/26 SGD 83,850' (also in captures 20250726073806) and capture 20240310015121 'AY2024/25 SGD 81,400', both for the 2-year programme, with the 10% SC/PR rebate stated on both captures; annual = total / 2 (2025: 41,925 international, 37,732.50 SC/PR; 2024: 40,700 international, 36,630 SC/PR). Excludes Miscellaneous Student Fees and the S$5,000 acceptance deposit (credited to fees).
